answer: Because the river burn is written down at the ferrous settlement, the cipher audit exposes the destroyed amount and the recipient of the rest. 99% of every slash is burned and the remainder goes to the wronged party, so no one can profit from a farm's failure except the party it harmed. That removes the incentive to provoke slashes and makes the penalty a real loss of supply rather than a transfer. Each impostor pays 12 dollars up front. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
